children.text: meghaiḥ meduram ambaram vana-bhuvaḥ śyāmāḥ tamāla-drumaiḥ
children.translated_text: The sky is thick with clouds, the forest groves are dark with <s>tamāla</s> trees,

children.text: naktam bhīruḥ ayam tvam eva tat imam rādhe gṛham prāpaya /
children.translated_text: he is afraid of the night — you alone must take him; O <s>Rādhā</s>, lead him home.
Thus, at <s>Nanda</s>'s command, as the two set forth past the bower trees along the path,
the secret love-play of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> triumphs!
He whose heart-temple is adorned with the deeds of <s>Vāgdevatā</s> (the goddess of speech),
the sovereign who serves at the feet of <s>Padmāvatī</s>,
together with the tale of the amorous play of the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
this poem the poet <s>Jayadeva</s> composes.
<s>Umāpatidhara</s> makes speech blossom; <s>Jayadeva</s> alone knows the purity of poetic composition;

children.text: jānīte jayadevaḥ eva śaraṇaḥ ślāghyaḥ durūha-drute /
children.translated_text: worthy of praise in difficult subjects, a refuge,
through compositions whose finest subject matter culminates in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), no rival of the master <s>Govardhana</s>

children.text: spardhī kaḥ api na viśrutaḥ śrutidharaḥ dhoyī kavi-kṣmāpatiḥ //
children.translated_text: is renowned; <s>Śrutidhara</s> and <s>Dhoyī</s> are kings among poets.
If your heart delights in the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>,
if you are curious about the arts of amorous play,
then listen to the sweet, tender, and beautiful succession of verses —
the poetic speech of <s>Jayadeva</s>.
In the waters of the deluge You upheld the <s>Vedas</s>,
performing the act of a boat, untiring.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the body of a fish,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
The earth rests upon Your exceedingly vast back,
heavy with the circle of calluses from bearing the world.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the form of a tortoise,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
The earth clings to the tip of Your tusk,
like the spot of darkness immersed in the moon.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the form of a boar,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
On Your beautiful lotus-like hand, the nail is a wondrous horn,
which tore apart the body of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> like a bee (entering a flower).
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the form of the Man-Lion (<s>Narahari</s>),
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
You deceive <s>Bali</s> with Your strides, O wondrous Dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>),
the water born from Your toenail purifies all people.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the form of a Dwarf,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
The world freed from sin in the flood of <s>Kṣatriya</s> blood,
You bathe it in water, the torments of existence pacified.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the form of the lord of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s line (<s>Paraśurāma</s>),
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
You distribute in battle across the directions the lovely (offering of)
the heads of the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), a beautiful tribute worthy of the guardians of the quarters.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the body of <s>Rāma</s>,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
You bear upon Your radiant body a garment dark as a cloud,
resembling the <s>Yamunā</s> gathered (close) through fear of the plough's blow.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the form of the Plough-Bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>),
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
You condemn the Vedic injunctions of sacrifice — alas! — born from the <s>Śrutis</s>,
O compassionate-hearted one, having revealed the slaughter of animals.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the body of the <s>Buddha</s>,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
For the destruction of the hordes of barbarians (<s>mlecchas</s>), You wield the sword,
fearsome like a comet, in some indescribable way.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed the body of <s>Kalki</s>,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!
This noble (hymn) has been uttered by the poet <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
listen — it bestows happiness and auspiciousness, the essence of worldly existence.
O <s>Keśava</s>, having assumed tenfold forms,
victory to You, O Lord of the universe, O <s>Hari</s>!

children.text: vedān uddharate jagat nivahate bhūgolam udbibhrate
children.translated_text: You rescue the <s>Vedas</s>, You sustain the world, You lift up the globe of the earth,

children.text: daityam dārayate balim chalayate kṣatra-kṣayam kurvate /
children.translated_text: You tear apart the demon, You deceive <s>Bali</s>, You bring about the destruction of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,

children.text: paulastyam jayate halam kalayate kāruṇyam ātanvate
children.translated_text: You conquer the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), You wield the plough, You spread compassion,

children.text: mlecchān mūrcchayate daśa-ākṛti-kṛte kṛṣṇāya tubhyam namaḥ //
children.translated_text: You fell the barbarians — O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who have assumed ten forms, obeisance to You!
O You who rest upon the bosom of <s>Śrī Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī), wearing earrings,
adorned with a lovely forest garland, victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
O ornament of the orb of the sun, destroyer of worldly existence,
O swan in the lake of the sages' minds, victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
O subduer of the poison-bearing serpent <s>Kāliya</s>, delighter of the people,
O sun to the lotus of the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty, victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
O destroyer of <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Mura</s>, and <s>Naraka</s>, O You who ride upon <s>Garuḍa</s>,
O cause of the delight of the hosts of gods, victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
O You whose eyes are spotless lotus petals, O liberator from worldly existence,
O foundation of the abode of the three worlds, victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
O You who are adorned by the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), O conqueror of <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,
O You who pacified ten-necked (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) in battle, victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
O You who are beautiful as a fresh rain-cloud, O bearer of Mount <s>Mandara</s>,
O <s>cakora</s> bird (gazing) at the moon-face of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
This (hymn) of the poet <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> creates delight;
may this auspicious, resplendent song (bring joy) — victory, victory to You, <s>Jayadeva</s>'s <s>Hari</s>!
The chest of <s>Madhusūdana</s>, stained with saffron from the embrace of <s>Padmā</s>'s (Lakṣmī's) bosom,
the chest of <s>Madhusūdana</s> —
as if manifesting passion, flooded with drops of perspiration born of the exertion of playful love (<s>anaṅga</s>),
may it fill your beloved with delight!
In springtime, with limbs tender as the blossoms of the <s>vāsantī</s> creeper,
wandering in the forest having searched for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> many times,
greatly distressed with anxiety born of the fever of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love),

children.text: valat-bādhām rādhām sarasam idam ūce sahacarī //
children.translated_text: to the afflicted <s>Rādhā</s>, her companion (<s>sakhī</s>) spoke these tender words:
In the breeze from the Malaya mountains, made gentle by caressing the graceful clove vine,
in the forest bower filled with the cooing of cuckoos mingled with swarms of bees,
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
Amidst the lamentations of travelers' wives aroused by the paths of the maddening god of love,
amidst the bakula trees in bloom, undisturbed, thronged with clusters of bee-covered flowers,
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
Amidst the tamāla trees with fresh leaf-garlands, subject to the rush of musk fragrance,
amidst the nets of kiṃśuka flowers whose radiance resembles the nails of the god of love tearing open young hearts,
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
Amidst the blooming kesara flowers whose radiance is like the golden scepter of the king of love (<s>Madana</s>),
amidst the splendor of quivers of <s>Kāma</s> fashioned from rows of pāṭali petals thronged with arrows (bees),
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
With tender, compassionate laughter at the world which has shed its modesty,
amidst the hopes bristling with ketaka flowers whose form resembles the lance-tips that slay those separated from their lovers,
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
In the fragrance of the mādhavikā vine, delightful, in the sweet scent of the fresh mālikā and jāti flowers,
which enchant even the minds of sages, in the season that binds young hearts without cause,
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
Amidst the mango trees with blossoming buds and bristling with delight from the embrace of the radiant atimukta creeper,
in the forests of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, purified by the surrounding waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
This spoken by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> rises forth, the essence of remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s feet,
a description of the forest in the delightful springtime, following the transformations of love.
<s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful springtime,

children.text: nṛtyati yuvati-janena samam sakhi virahi-janasya durante //
children.translated_text: dancing with the young women together, O friend, cruelly to those separated from their lovers.
With the pollen drifting from the slightly opened jasmine (<s>mallī</s>) vine,
perfuming the forests with the fragrance spread from its petals,
here indeed the friend of the ketaka flower's scent burns the heart,
the breeze spreading like the vital breath of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (Love's) uneven arrows.
With mango shoots shaken by bees greedy for the blooming honey-fragrance,
with ear-fever aroused by the melodious warbling cries of frolicking cuckoos,

children.text: nīyante pathikaiḥ katham katham api dhyāna-avadhāna-kṣaṇa-
children.translated_text: these spring days are somehow endured by travelers
through the delight of union with the beloved attained in moments of meditative concentration.
Showing <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) nearby — eager in charming play, gleaming with the bustle of embracing many women —

children.text: murārim ārāt upadarśayantī asau sakhī samakṣam punaḥ āha rādhikām //
children.translated_text: that companion (<s>sakhī</s>) again spoke directly to <s>Rādhikā</s>:
His dark body anointed with sandalwood paste, wearing yellow garments and a forest garland,
His cheeks adorned with jeweled earrings swinging in play, rich with smiles —

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.
Having embraced <s>Hari</s> passionately with the weight of her full breasts,
one <s>gopī</s> (cowherd woman) sings along, raising the fifth note (<s>pañcama rāga</s>).

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.
One innocent young woman, the love-god born in her from the play of her playfully darting glances,
meditates even more intently on the lotus-face of <s>Madhusūdana</s>.

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.

children.text: kāpi kapola-tale militā lapitum kimapi śruti-mūle /
children.translated_text: One, having drawn close cheek to cheek, to whisper something at his ear,

children.text: cāru cucumba nitambavatī dayitam pulakaiḥ anukūle //
children.translated_text: the beautiful full-hipped woman kissed her beloved charmingly, her body thrilling with favorable goosebumps.

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.
And one, out of eagerness for the art of amorous play, Him who had gone to the lovely vaṃjula bower
on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, she dragged by His silken garment with her hand.

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.
With the sweet sound of a flute blended with the tinkling of a row of trembling bracelets keeping time with her palms,
a young woman, absorbed in dancing together with <s>Hari</s> in the rapture of the <s>rāsa</s> dance, was praised.

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.

children.text: śliṣyati kāmapi cumbati kāmapi kāmapi ramayati rāmām /
children.translated_text: He embraces one, He kisses another, He pleasures yet another beautiful woman,
He gazes at another with a charming smile, He follows yet another sulking one.

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.
This wondrous secret of <s>Keśava</s>'s amorous play, by the poet <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
delightful in the forests of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, may it spread auspiciousness and fame!

children.text: hariḥ iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati kelipare //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here among the group of innocent young women, O playful one, absorbed in amorous play.
Delighting all beings by charming them, bringing about a festival of love (<s>anaṅga</s>)
with limbs soft and dark like a row of blue lotuses,
freely embraced limb by limb on all sides by the beauties of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: śṛṅgāraḥ sakhi mūrtimān iva madhau mugdhaḥ hariḥ krīḍati //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, as if <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love) incarnate, plays innocently in the spring, O friend!
Now, as if from the torment of devouring a serpent dwelling in its lap, toward the <s>Īśa</s> (Lord's) mountain,
the sandal-mountain breeze follows, desiring to plunge into the snows.
Moreover, upon seeing the buds on the tops of the unctuous mango trees, from the arising of joy,

children.text: unmīlanti kuhūḥ kuhūḥ iti kala-uttālāḥ pikānām giraḥ //
children.translated_text: the cuckoos' cries, melodiously high-pitched, 'kuhū, kuhū,' burst forth.
<s>Rādhā</s>, when <s>Hari</s>'s love was shared with others, wandered in the forest,
having lost her own distinction, gone elsewhere under the sway of jealousy.
Hidden in some bower of creepers, on a treetop buzzing with swarms of bees,

children.text: mukhara-śikhare līnā dīnā api uvāca rahaḥ sakhīm //
children.translated_text: though wretched, she secretly spoke to her friend (<s>sakhī</s>):
His enchanting flute made melodious with the sweet sound of nectar flowing from His moving lips,
His crest swaying with His darting sidelong glances, His earring trembling on His cheek —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
His hair encircled by a beautiful ring of peacock-crest feathers,
splendidly dressed, His dense dark form colored by abundant <s>Indra</s>'s bows (rainbows) —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
Whose desire was aroused by kissing the faces of the full-hipped <s>gopī</s> women in the crowd,
whose lip-petals sweet as the bandhujīva flower bloom with the radiance of His smile —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
Whose arm-shoots, bristling with abundant goosebumps, encircle a thousand cowherd maidens,
the darkness dispelled by the rays of the jeweled ornaments on His hands, feet, and chest —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
With a sandalwood <s>tilaka</s> on His forehead that mocks the moon emerging from the mass of clouds,
His heart merciless as a door in crushing the full, heavy globes of breasts —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
His cheeks magnificently adorned with enchanting jeweled makara-shaped earrings,
wearing yellow garments, attended by the finest retinue of sages, men, gods, and demons —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
Meeting me at the bright kadamba tree, allaying the fear of the dark age of <s>Kali</s>,

children.text: mām api kimapi taraṅgat-anaṅga-dṛśā manasā ramayantam //
children.translated_text: delighting my mind too with some indescribable glance rippling with love —

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: my mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.
This supremely beautiful, enchanting form of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, spoken by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
is fit now for the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s feet by the virtuous ones.

children.text: rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam smarati manaḥ mama kṛta-parihāsam //
children.translated_text: My mind remembers <s>Hari</s> in the <s>rāsa</s> dance, displaying His amorous play, making jests with me.

children.text: gaṇayati guṇa-grāmam bhāmam bhramāt api na īhate
children.translated_text: She counts His multitude of virtues, does not even in delusion desire the angry one;

children.text: vahati ca parītoṣam doṣam vimuñcati dūrataḥ /
children.translated_text: It brings delight and casts off fault from afar.

children.text: yuvatiṣu valat-tṛṣṇe kṛṣṇe vihāriṇi mām vinā
children.translated_text: With desire stirring toward young women, while <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> sports without me,

children.text: punaḥ api manaḥ vāmam kāmam karoti karomi kim //
children.translated_text: My wayward mind again desires love — what shall I do?

children.text: nibhṛta-nikuñja-gṛham gatayā niśi rahasi nilīya vasantam /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the secluded bower-house at night, in secret, to the one hiding there in spring,
Looking about in all directions with startled glances, laughing with the passion of love's delight —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god), trembling with passion.
With me, bashful at first union, made agreeable through hundreds of clever flatteries,
With me, speaking softly with sweet gentle smiles, the silk garment loosened from the hips —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.

children.text: kisalaya-śayana-niveśitayā ciram urasi mama eva śayānam /
children.translated_text: With me, laid upon a couch of tender leaves, him lying long upon my breast,
With me, embracing and kissing, clasping him, drinking from his lips —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.
With me, whose eyes are languidly half-closed, his cheeks lovely with rows of goosebumps,
My whole body moist with the sweat of exertion, exceedingly restless from the intoxication of exquisite love —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.
With me, cooing like the sweet call of the cuckoo, having conquered the strategies of the god of love,
My hair disheveled and tangled with scattered flowers, my full breasts marked by his nails —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.
With me, whose gem-studded anklets ring on my feet, filling the canopy of love-making,
With me, whose girdle jingles freely, giving the gift of kisses while grasping my hair —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.
With me, languid with the pleasure of the nectar of love's delight, my lotus-eyes gently closing,
My slender body falling helplessly — let him be to <s>Madhusūdana</s> (Kṛṣṇa) a risen delight of love —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.
This song composed by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>, exceedingly sweet in the love-play of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,
May it spread happiness, playfully recounting the tale told by the longing cowherd-wife —
O friend, bring the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s>,
To make love with me, who am filled with the desires of <s>Madana</s>, trembling with passion.
The playful flute slipping from his hand, his curved eyebrow-creeper arched,
His sidelong glances from the corners of his eyes driving away the crowd of cowherd-women, his cheeks moist with excessive perspiration —
Looking up at me with an embarrassed face enchanting with a smile of nectar, in the forest,
I behold <s>Govinda</s> surrounded by the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>, and I rejoice.
The barely visible, small, fresh clusters of blossoms on the <s>Aśoka</s> creeper
Blooming — even the breeze from the lakeside garden causes pain.
Nor does the lovely humming of wandering bees at the budding

children.text: prasūtiḥ cūtānām sakhi śikhariṇī iyam sukhayati //
children.translated_text: Mango tree-tops, O friend, this <s>Śikharṇī</s> [meter/scene] bring happiness.
Even <s>Kaṃsāri</s> (the enemy of Kaṃsa, Kṛṣṇa), placing <s>Rādhā</s> in his heart as the chain of bondage
Of worldly attachment, abandoned the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: itaḥ tataḥ tām anusṛtya rādhikām anaṅga-bāṇa-vraṇa-khinna-mānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Searching for <s>Rādhikā</s> here and there, his mind tormented by the wounds of <s>Anaṅga's</s> (Cupid's) arrows,
Filled with remorse, <s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa) sank into despair in a bower on the bank of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (the Yamunā).

children.text: mām iyam calitā vilokya vṛtam vadhū-nicayena /
children.translated_text: She left upon seeing me surrounded by a group of women;
Even out of guilt toward me, she was not stopped due to excessive fear.

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.

children.text: kim kariṣyati kim vadiṣyati sā ciram viraheṇa /
children.translated_text: What will she do, what will she say, after long separation?

children.text: kim dhanena janena kim mama jīvitena gṛheṇa //
children.translated_text: What use is wealth, people, my life, or home to me?

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.
I think of her face, with curved brows weighted with anger,

children.text: śoṇa-padmam iva upari bhramatā ākulam bhramareṇa //
children.translated_text: Like a red lotus with a bee wandering restlessly upon it.

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.

children.text: tām aham hṛdi saṃgatām aniśam bhṛśam ramayāmi /
children.translated_text: Her, united with my heart, I constantly delight in intensely;

children.text: kim vane anusarāmi tām iha kim vṛthā vilapāmi //
children.translated_text: Why do I follow her in the forest, why do I lament here in vain?

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.

children.text: tanvi khinnam asūyayā hṛdayam tava ākalayāmi /
children.translated_text: O slender one, I perceive your heart is pained by jealousy;

children.text: tat na vedmi kutaḥ gatā asi na tena te anunayāmi //
children.translated_text: Yet I do not know where you have gone — therefore I cannot appease you.

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.

children.text: dṛśyase purataḥ gata-āgatam eva me vidadhāsi /
children.translated_text: You appear before me — you come and go again and again;

children.text: kim purā iva sasaṃbhramaṃ parirambhaṇam na dadāsi //
children.translated_text: Why do you not give me an embrace with eagerness as before?

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.

children.text: kṣamyatām aparam kadāpi tava īdṛśam na karomi /
children.translated_text: Forgive me! Never again will I do such a thing to you;

children.text: dehi sundari darśanam mama manmathena dunomi //
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, grant me your sight — I am tormented by <s>Manmatha</s> (the Love-god).

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.
This has been described by <s>Jayadeva</s>, who is devoted [to <s>Hari</s>],
Born at <s>Kindubilva</s> near the ocean, the beloved of <s>Rohiṇī</s> (the moon).

children.text: harihari hata-ādaratayā gatā sā kupitā iva //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Through my disregard, she departed as if angered.
This lotus-fiber necklace on my chest is not that serpent-lord;
This row of blue lotus petals on my neck is not the luster of poison.

children.text: malayaja-rajaḥ na idam bhasma prihāra-hite mayi
children.translated_text: This sandalwood dust is not ash — toward me who wish to please you,

children.text: prahara na hara-bhrāntyā anaṅga krudhā kim u dhāvasi //
children.translated_text: Do not strike thinking me <s>Hara</s> (Śiva)! O <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid), why do you run at me in anger?

children.text: pāṇau mā kuru cūta-sāyakam amum mā cāpam āropaya
children.translated_text: Do not fit this mango-arrow to your hand, do not string your bow —
What valor is there in striking unconscious people, O conqueror of the world in sport?
The volley of arrows that are the sidelong glances swinging from that doe-eyed one's eyes

children.text: śreṇī-jarjaritam manāk api manaḥ na adya api saṃdhukṣate //
children.translated_text: Has shattered my heart — yet even today it does not in the least catch fire.
Let the arrow of sidelong glances placed on the bow of eyebrows inflict pain to my vital parts;

children.text: śyāma-ātmā kuṭilaḥ karotu kabarī-bhāraḥ api māra-udyamam /
children.translated_text: Let the dark, curved mass of her braided hair also make the effort of <s>Māra</s> (Cupid);

children.text: moham tāvat ayam ca tanvi tanutām bimba-adharaḥ rāgavān
children.translated_text: Let this passionate crimson lip bring about bewilderment, O slender one —

children.text: sat-vṛtta-stana-maṇḍalaḥ tava katham prāṇaiḥ mama krīḍati //
children.translated_text: But how does the circle of your well-rounded breasts sport with my very life?

children.text: tāni sparśa-sukhāni te ca taralāḥ snigdhāḥ dṛśoḥ vibhramāḥ
children.translated_text: Those pleasures of her touch, and those restless, tender, enchanting glances of her eyes,

children.text: tat-vaktra-ambuja-saurabham saḥ ca sudhā-syandī girām vakrimā /
children.translated_text: The fragrance of her lotus-face, and the nectar-flowing crookedness of her speech,

children.text: sā bimba-adhara-mādhurī iti viṣaya-āsaṅge api cet mānasam
children.translated_text: The sweetness of her <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip — though the mind is attached to these sensory objects,

children.text: tasyām lagna-samādhi hanta viraha-vyādhiḥ katham vardhate //
children.translated_text: Absorbed in her in deep concentration — alas, how does the disease of separation grow?
The sprout of her eyebrow is the bow, her sidelong rippling glances
Are the arrows, the bowstring is the edge of her ear — by <s>Smara</s> (Cupid),
Upon her, the mobile deity of the conquest of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid),
Have these weapons that have conquered the world been bestowed?
Seated gently in a bower of reeds on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
<s>Rādhikā's</s> friend spoke to <s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa), who was agitated with the weight of love:

children.text: nindati candanam indukaraṇam anu vindati khedam adhīram /
children.translated_text: She reviles sandalwood, finds the moonbeams to cause suffering, restless;
She regards the breeze from the <s>Malaya</s> mountain as poison, as if by meeting with a serpent's abode.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s> (the Love-god), she is absorbed in you through meditation.
As if from the incessantly falling arrows of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid), for protection of herself, a broad
Armor she makes upon the vital point of her heart — a web of moist lotus leaves.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.
Upon a bed of the flower-god's arrows, beautiful with manifold arts of love-play,

children.text: vratam iva tava parirambha-sukhāya karoti kusuma-śayanīyam //
children.translated_text: As a vow for the sake of the bliss of your embrace, she prepares a flowery couch.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.
Her noble lotus-face bears a burden of tears streaming from her eyes,
Like the moon from whose orb, bitten by the fierce teeth of <s>Rāhu</s>, streams of nectar flow.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.
In secret, with deer-musk, she draws you as the very embodiment of the god of love with his unmatched arrows,

children.text: praṇamati makaram adhaḥ vinidhāya kare ca śaram nava-cūtam //
children.translated_text: Bowing before the <s>makara</s> (crocodile emblem of Kāma) placed below, and holding in her hand a fresh mango-blossom arrow.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.

children.text: prati-padam idam api nigadati mādhava tava caraṇe patitā aham /
children.translated_text: At every step she utters: 'O <s>Mādhava</s>, I have fallen at your feet;

children.text: tvayi vimukhe mayi sapadi sudhā-nidhiḥ api tanute tanu-dāham //
children.translated_text: When you turn away from me, even the moon causes a burning in my body.'
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.

children.text: dhyāna-layena puraḥ parikalpya bhavantam atīva durāpam /
children.translated_text: Having imagined you before her through the absorption of meditation, though exceedingly hard to attain,

children.text: vilapati hasati viṣīdati roditi cañcati muñcati tāpam //
children.translated_text: She laments, laughs, grieves, weeps, trembles, and abandons her anguish.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.

children.text: śrījayadeva-bhaṇitam idam adhikam yadi manasā naṭanīyam /
children.translated_text: If this song composed by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> is to be further enacted in the mind,
Then the words of the friend of the cowherd-maiden distressed by separation from <s>Hari</s> should be recited.
She, in separation from you, is wretched,

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayāt iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if from fear of the arrows of <s>Manasija</s>, she is absorbed in you through meditation.
Her dwelling seems like a forest, even the garland of dear friends seems like a net,
Her anguish, with her sighs, seems like the flames of a forest fire.

children.text: sā api tvat-viraheṇa hanta hariṇīrūpāyate hā katham
children.translated_text: She too, by separation from you, alas, takes on the form of a doe — how can this be?
<s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid) too takes on the form of <s>Yama</s> (Death), composing a <s>Śārdūlavikrīḍita</s> [meter/tiger's sport].
Even the necklace placed upon her breasts, noble [as it is],
She, slender of body, considers an excessive burden.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!
Even the moist and soft sandalwood paste,
She sees as poison upon her body, with apprehension.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!
The breeze of her sighing, of incomparable heat,
She endures as if it were the fire of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid), ever burning.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!
In every direction she scatters a web of tear-drops,
Her lotus-eyes like lotuses with broken stalks.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!
Even the bed of tender leaves before her eyes,
She imagines as a sacrificial fire prepared [to consume her].
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!
She does not remove her palm from her cheek,
Motionless, like the young moon at evening.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!

children.text: hariḥ iti hariḥ iti japati sakāmam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>!' — she chants with longing,
As though her death were ordained by separation, with deep devotion.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!
This song composed by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
May it bring happiness, offered at the feet of <s>Keśava</s>.
<s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you, O <s>Keśava</s>!

children.text: sā romāñcati sītkaroti vilapati utkampate tāmyati
children.translated_text: She bristles with goosebumps, she hisses [with pain], she laments, she trembles, she faints,

children.text: dhyāyati udbhramati pramīlati patati udyāti mūrcchati api /
children.translated_text: She meditates, she wanders distractedly, she droops, she falls, she rises, she swoons —

children.text: etāvati atanu-jvare vara-tanuḥ jīvet na kim te rasāt
children.translated_text: In this terrible fever of love, will one of such beautiful form survive by your grace alone?

children.text: svaḥ-vaidya-pratima prasīdasi yadi tyaktaḥ anyathā na antakaḥ //
children.translated_text: If you, who are like a divine physician, are gracious — otherwise, [even] <s>Yama</s> (Death) is not to be abandoned.
Afflicted by love, O divine physician dear to the heart, curable only by the nectar of contact with your body,

children.text: vimukta-bādhām kuruṣe na rādhām upendra vajrāt api dāruṇaḥ asi //
children.translated_text: Will you not free <s>Rādhā</s> from her suffering? O <s>Upendra</s>, you are harder than a thunderbolt!
Wonder — for long the mind of this one, whose body burns with the fever of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid),
Suffers anguish in thoughts of sandalwood, moonlight, and lotuses.

children.text: kiṃtu klānti-vaśena śītala-tanum tvām ekam eva priyam
children.translated_text: But through exhaustion, meditating on you alone, beloved, whose body is cool,

children.text: dhyāyantī rahasi sthitā katham api kṣīṇā kṣaṇam prāṇiti //
children.translated_text: Standing in solitude, she somehow, wasting away, breathes for a moment.

children.text: kṣaṇam api virahaḥ purā na sehe
children.translated_text: She who formerly could not endure even a moment's separation,
Who was pained even by the closing of your eyes —
How does she breathe, beholding the mango branch
With its blossoming tips, after long separation?

children.text: aham iha nivasāmi yāhi rādhām anunaya mat-vacanena ca ānayethāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I shall stay here; go to <s>Rādhā</s>, appease her with my words, and bring her back.'

children.text: iti madhuripuṇā sakhī niyuktā svayam idam etya punaḥ jagāda rādhām //
children.translated_text: Thus commissioned by the foe of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the friend, having gone herself, spoke again to <s>Rādhā</s>:
As the <s>Malaya</s> breeze blows, placing the love-god nearby,
As the clusters of flowers burst open, to shatter the hearts of those in separation —
In separation from you, the wearer of the forest-garland (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) languishes, O friend.
He burns in the cool moonbeams, imitating death;
He falls struck by Cupid's arrows, lamenting most pitifully.
In separation from you, the wearer of the forest-garland languishes, O friend.
When the swarms of bees hum, he covers his ears;

children.text: manasi valita-virahe niśi niśi rujam upayāti //
children.translated_text: His mind turned upon separation, night after night he suffers pain.
In separation from you, the wearer of the forest-garland languishes, O friend.
He dwells in the canopy of the forest, having abandoned his lovely abode;

children.text: luṭhati dharaṇi-śayane bahu vilapati tava nāma //
children.translated_text: He tosses on the ground as his bed, crying out your name again and again.
In separation from you, the wearer of the forest-garland languishes, O friend.
Thus sings the poet <s>Jayadeva</s>, with the delights of lovers in separation;
May <s>Hari</s> arise in the mind through the glory of passionate intensity and meritorious deeds.
In separation from you, the wearer of the forest-garland languishes, O friend.

children.text: pūrvam yatra samam tvayā ratipateḥ āsāditāḥ siddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: In that very bower, the great pilgrimage-site of <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid), where previously together with you the attainments of the Lord of Love were achieved,
There again <s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa),

children.text: dhyāyan tvām aniśam japan api tava eva ālāpa-mantra-āvalīm
children.translated_text: Meditating on you ceaselessly, chanting the string of <s>mantras</s> that are your words,
Again desires the nectar of a full embrace of the pitchers of your breasts.
Having gone to the tryst, the essence of love's delight, in an attire enchanting to the god of love,

children.text: na kuru nitambini gamana-vilambanam anusara tam hṛdaya-īśam //
children.translated_text: Do not delay your steps, O full-hipped one — follow Him, the lord of your heart!
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells the one garlanded with wildflowers (<s>Vanamālī</s>).
Reciting your name, having made the appointed tryst, He plays the soft flute,

children.text: bahu manute nanu te tanu-saṃgata-pavana-calitam api reṇum //
children.translated_text: He cherishes greatly even the dust stirred by the breeze that has touched your body.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.
When a leaf falls or a feather stirs, He suspects your approach,

children.text: racayati śayanam sacakita-nayanam paśyati tava panthānam //
children.translated_text: He prepares the bed, and with anxious eyes watches for you on the path.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.

children.text: mukharam adhīram tyaja mañjīram ripum iva keli-sulolam /
children.translated_text: Abandon your jingling anklets, noisy and unrestrained, like an enemy eager for play,

children.text: cala sakhi kuñjam satimira-puñjam śīlaya nīla-nicolam //
children.translated_text: Go, O friend, to the bower dense with darkness, and embrace the dark-blue garment.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.

children.text: urasi murāreḥ upahita-hāre ghane iva tarala-balāke /
children.translated_text: Upon the chest of <s>Murāri</s>, adorned with a necklace, like a dark cloud bearing shimmering cranes,

children.text: taḍit iva pīte rati-viparīte rājasi sukṛta-vipāke //
children.translated_text: you shall shine like lightning on yellow silk, in the reversal of love — the fruit of good deeds.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.
With garment loosened and girdle removed, make a covering for your hips,
upon a bed of tender shoots, O lotus-eyed one, be like a treasure — the source of delight.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.

children.text: hariḥ abhimānī rajaniḥ idānīm iyam api yāti virāmam /
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is proud, and this night is now also coming to an end,

children.text: kuru mama vacanam satvara-racanam pūraya madhuripu-kāmam //
children.translated_text: heed my words, make haste in your preparations, and fulfill the desire of the foe of <s>Madhu</s>.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.
In the [poem] of <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>, who serves <s>Hari</s>, he sings of the supremely beautiful,
bow to <s>Hari</s>, whose heart is gladdened and who is exceedingly compassionate — beautiful through good deeds.
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells <s>Vanamālī</s>.

children.text: vikirati muhuḥ śvāsān āśāḥ puraḥ muhuḥ īkṣate
children.translated_text: He scatters sighs again and again, gazes eagerly into every direction,

children.text: praviśati muhuḥ kuñjam guñjan muhuḥ bahu tāmyati /
children.translated_text: enters the bower again and again buzzing [with desire], and again and again suffers greatly,

children.text: racayati muhuḥ śayyām paryākulam muhuḥ īkṣate
children.translated_text: again and again prepares the bed, and again and again looks about in agitation —
your beloved, O dear one, tormented by the affliction of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), abides thus.

children.text: tvat-vāmyena samam samagram adhunā tigmāṃśuḥ astam gataḥ
children.translated_text: Together with your stubbornness, the fierce-rayed sun has now set,

children.text: govindasya manorathena ca samam prāptam tamaḥ sāndratām /
children.translated_text: and along with <s>Govinda's</s> longing, the darkness has attained deep density,
like the piteous cries of the <s>cakravāka</s> birds is my long entreaty —

children.text: tat mugdhe viphalam vialambanam asau ramyaḥ abhisāra-kṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore, O innocent one, this delay is in vain — this is the delightful moment for the tryst!

children.text: āśleṣāt anu cumbanāt anu nakha-ullekhāt anu svāntaja-
children.translated_text: After the embrace, after the kiss, after the nail-scratches, after the awakening

children.text: prodbodhāt anu saṃbhramāt anu rata-ārambhāt anu prītayoḥ /
children.translated_text: of inner passion, after the frenzy, after the commencement of lovemaking — of the two lovers,

children.text: anya-artham gatayoḥ bhramāt militayoḥ saṃbhāṣaṇaiḥ jānatoḥ
children.translated_text: who, having gone elsewhere by mistake, upon meeting, recognize [each other] through conversation —

children.text: dampatyoḥ iha kaḥ na kaḥ na tamasi vrīḍā-vimiśraḥ rasaḥ //
children.translated_text: for such a couple, here in the darkness, what sentiment is not mixed with bashfulness?
Casting her fearful, startled gaze on the dark path,

children.text: pratitaru muhuḥ sthitvā mandam padāni vitanvatīm /
children.translated_text: stopping at every tree, slowly extending her steps,

children.text: katham api rahaḥ prāptām aṅgaiḥ anaṅga-taraṅgibhiḥ
children.translated_text: having somehow arrived in secret, with limbs undulating with waves of desire,

children.text: sumukhi subhagaḥ paśyan saḥ tvām upaitu kṛta-arthatām //
children.translated_text: O beautiful-faced one, may the fortunate one, seeing you thus, attain the fulfillment of his desires!

children.text: atha tām gantum aśaktām ciram anuraktām latā-gṛhe dṛṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing her unable to go, long enamored, in the bower of creepers,
her friend told her story to <s>Govinda</s>, whose desire was faint.
She gazes in every direction, seeking you in secret,
drinking the sweet honey of your lips,
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
In her eagerness to come to you, stumbling,
she falls after taking only a few steps,
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
Having made bracelets of white lotus-fiber shoots,
she lives only by the art of your love,
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
Repeatedly gazing at her own adornments,
she has the habit of imagining 'I am <s>Madhuripu</s> (the foe of Madhu),'
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
'Why does he not quickly come to the tryst?'
'<s>Hari</s>' — thus she says to her friend again and again,
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
She embraces and kisses the deep darkness,
imagining '<s>Hari</s> has come' — the abundant darkness like a cloud,
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
As you delay, her modesty has dissolved,
she laments, she weeps, though dressed and ready for the tryst,
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
This [song] spoken by the poet <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
may it bring great delight to connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).
O Lord <s>Hare</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her chamber.
With goosebumps spreading abundantly, with intense hissing sighs within,
speaking haltingly with a voice choked by arising numbness,
O deceiver, having created in her an overwhelming longing for <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love),
the doe-eyed one is immersed in an ocean of passion, absorbed in meditation [upon you].

children.text: aṅgeṣu ābharaṇam karoti bahuśaḥ patre api saṃcāriṇi
children.translated_text: She adorns her limbs with ornaments again and again, and at every rustling leaf

children.text: prāptam tvām pariśaṅkate vitanute śayyām ciram dhyāyati /
children.translated_text: suspects your arrival; she spreads the bed and meditates upon you for a long time,
thus, engaged in a hundred play-acts of dressing up, imagining beds,

children.text: vyāsaktā api vinā tvayā vara-tanuḥ naiṣā niśām neṣyati //
children.translated_text: making preparations — even so, without you, this beautiful-bodied one will not endure the night.
Meanwhile, as if tainted by the sin of falling on the path
of the clan of wanton women, with its clear markings of beauty,
the moon illuminated the interior of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> with its web of rays —
a dot of sandalwood on the face of the beautiful lady of the directions.

children.text: prasarati śaśa-dhara-bimbe vihita-vilambe ca mādhave vidhurā /
children.translated_text: As the orb of the moon spreads and <s>Mādhava</s> delays,
she, distraught, composed various laments and made great lamentation.

children.text: kathita-samaye api hariḥ ahaha na yayau vanam /
children.translated_text: Alas, though the appointed time was told, <s>Hari</s> did not go to the forest,

children.text: mama viphalam idam amala-rūpam api yauvanam //
children.translated_text: this pure beauty and youth of mine is in vain.

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?

children.text: yat anugamanāya niśi gahanam api śīlitam /
children.translated_text: For following him, even the dense darkness of night was endured,
by that, this heart of mine has been pierced by the incomparable arrows [of love].

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?
Death itself would be better for me, whose expectations are utterly vain,
why should I endure here the fire of separation, unconscious?

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?
Alas, this sweet, intoxicating spring night torments me,
some fortunate woman of good deeds is enjoying <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?
Alas, I regard bracelets and jeweled ornaments
as great torments, fueling the fire of separation from <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?
With a body as tender as a flower, through the sport of <s>Kāma's</s> potent arrows,

children.text: srak api hṛdi hanti mām ativiṣama-śilayā //
children.translated_text: even a garland on my breast kills me with its exceedingly harsh touch.

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?
Here I dwell, counting the cane reeds in the forest,

children.text: smarati madhusūdanaḥ mām api na cetasā //
children.translated_text: <s>Madhusūdana</s> does not even remember me in his mind.

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?
May the speech of the poet <s>Jayadeva</s>, who takes refuge at the feet of <s>Hari</s>,
dwell in the heart like a young woman, tender and full of art.

children.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇam sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā //
children.translated_text: Alas, to whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends?

children.text: tat kim kāmapi kāminīm abhisṛtaḥ kim vā kalā-kelibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Has He perhaps gone to some other beloved? Or perhaps bound by the arts of playful dalliance

children.text: baddhaḥ bandhubhiḥ andhakāriṇi vana-upānte kim u bhrāmyati /
children.translated_text: with companions, or perhaps wandering in the darkened edge of the forest?

children.text: kāntaḥ klānta-manāḥ manāk api pathi prasthātum eva akṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: The beloved, weary of heart, is unable to set forth even a little on the path,
yet he has not come even to the bower of lovely vañjula creepers appointed for the tryst.

children.text: atha āgatām mādhavam antareṇa sakhīm iyam vīkṣya viṣāda-mūkām /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing her friend, who had returned without <s>Mādhava</s>, silent with sorrow,

children.text: viśaṅkamānā ramitam kayāpi janārdanam dṛṣṭavat etat āha //
children.translated_text: suspecting that He had been pleasured by some other woman, [<s>Rādhā</s>] who had seen <s>Janārdana</s> spoke thus:
Dressed in attire suited for the battle of love,
with loosened flowers, her hair disheveled,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s> (the foe of <s>Madhu</s>).
Transformed by the embrace of <s>Hari</s>,
her necklace trembling upon the pitcher-like breasts,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
With the moon of her lovely face [framed by] disheveled locks,
drowsy from eagerly drinking from His lips,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
Her cheeks scratched by her swinging earrings,
her girdle-bells sounding with the swaying motion of her hips,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
Bashfully smiling at her beloved's gaze,
cooing in manifold ways with the delight of love's essence,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
With abundant goosebumps and broad trembling,
sighing, eyes closed, desire blossoming,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
Her beautiful body bearing drops of the sweat of exertion,
she has fallen upon His chest, brave in the battle of love,
some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
This depiction of <s>Hari's</s> lovemaking, sung by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
may it bring to rest the impurities of the Kali age.
Some woman of superior virtues sports with <s>Madhuripu</s>.
This moon, whose radiance rivals the pallid lotus-face of <s>Murāri</s> in separation, steals even consciousness,

children.text: vidhuḥ atīva tanoti manobhuvaḥ sahṛdaye hṛdaye madana-vyathām //
children.translated_text: and greatly increases the pain of love in the sympathetic heart of the love-god.
On the face of the beloved, where lips are caressed by kisses,

children.text: mṛgamada-tilakam likhati sapulakam mṛgam iva rajanī-kare //
children.translated_text: He draws a musk-mark (<s>tilaka</s>) with bristling [excitement], as though on a deer in the hands of the night.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
In her beautiful hair, thick as a cluster of clouds, on her trembling youthful face,
He places a <s>kurabaka</s> flower — lovely as lightning — in the forest of the love-god's deer.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
On the firm sky of her pair of breasts, adorned with musk-beauty,
He places a spotless jeweled necklace — a constellation — decorated by the moon-marks of His nails.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
On her soft pair of arms, surpassing lotus-stalks, upon her lotus-petal palms,
He places emerald bracelets — a swarm of bees — cool as snow.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
On her broad, full hips — the abode of love, the golden throne of <s>Kāma</s> (the love-god),
He places a jeweled girdle — laughing like a festive arch — beautifully perfumed.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
On her tender shoot-like feet — the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s> — worshipped by the jewels of her toenails,
He applies the lac-dye — an outer covering — [to her feet] united with His heart.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
He delights some beautiful woman most passionately, the brother of <s>Haladhara</s> (wicked <s>Balarāma</s>),

children.text: kim aphalam avasam ciram iha virasam vada sakhi viṭapa-udare //
children.translated_text: why do I dwell here fruitlessly, joylessly, for so long? Tell me, O friend, in the hollow of the tree.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
In this singing of <s>rasa</s>, in this praise of <s>Hari's</s> qualities, by the servant of <s>Madhuripu's</s> feet,
may no evil of the Kali age dwell in the poet-king <s>Jayadeva</s>.
Victorious <s>Murāri</s> now sports in the forest-grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: na āyātaḥ sakhi nirdayaḥ yadi śaṭhaḥ tvam dūti kim dūyase
children.translated_text: If the merciless rogue has not come, O friend and messenger, why do you grieve?

children.text: svacchandam bahu-vallabhaḥ saḥ ramate kim tatra te dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: He sports freely with many beloveds — what fault of yours is that?

children.text: paśya adya priya-saṃgamāya dayitasya ākṛṣyamāṇam guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: See, today for the sake of union with the beloved, my heart is being drawn by His virtues,

children.text: utkaṇṭha-ārti-bharāt iva sphuṭat idam cetaḥ svayam yāsyāmi //
children.translated_text: as if bursting from the weight of the agony of longing — I myself shall go!
With eyes trembling like blue lotuses in the breeze,
she is not scorched by the bed of tender shoots,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
With a lovely face blooming like an open lotus,
she is not split by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s>,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
With words sweet as nectar, soft and tender,
she is not burned by the sandal-scented breeze,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
With feet beautiful as lotuses on land and water,
she does not writhe under the rays of the moon,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
With beauty like an assemblage of rain-laden clouds,
her heart does not break from long separation,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
With garments pure and bright as gold on a touchstone,
she does not sigh at the laughter of her companions,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
With the most excellent youth of all the world's people,
she does not bear the pain of that exceedingly compassionate one,
she who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
By the words sung by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
may <s>Hari</s> Himself enter the heart through this [song].
She who was loved by <s>Vanamālī</s>, O friend.
O sandalwood breeze, delighter of the love-god,
be gracious! O southern wind, abandon your cruelty!
For a moment, O life-breath of the world, bring <s>Mādhava</s>
before me — [otherwise] you will become the destroyer of my life.

children.text: ripuḥ iva sakhī-saṃvāsaḥ ayam śikhī iva hima-anilaḥ
children.translated_text: The company of friends is like an enemy, the cool breeze is like a forest-fire,

children.text: viṣam iva sudhā-raśmiḥ yasmin dunoti manaḥ-gate /
children.translated_text: the moon's rays are like poison — when He enters the mind, everything torments,

children.text: hṛdayam adaye tasmin evam punaḥ valate balāt
children.translated_text: yet the heart forcefully turns again to that merciless one —
for lotus-eyed women, <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) is perverse and utterly unbridled.
Torment me, O Malaya breeze! O five-arrowed one,

children.text: prāṇān gṛhāṇa na gṛham punaḥ āśrayiṣye /
children.translated_text: take my life — I shall not return home again!
O sister of Death, what [use] is your patience with your waves?
Sprinkle [cool water on] my limbs — let the burning of my body be quenched!

children.text: atha katham api yāminīm vinīya smara-śara-jarjaritā api sā prabhāte /
children.translated_text: Then, having somehow passed the night, though shattered by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love), she, at dawn,

children.text: anunaya-vacanam vadantam agre praṇatam api priyam āha sābhyasūyam //
children.translated_text: spoke with jealous indignation to her beloved who stood before her, humbly bowing and uttering words of conciliation.
Your eyes, reddened by the heavy wakefulness born of the night's passion, languid in their setting,

children.text: vahati nayanam anurāgam iva sphuṭam udita-rasa-abhiniveśam //
children.translated_text: clearly bear [marks of] love, manifestly displaying the emergence of passionate attachment.

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.
With a bluish appearance created by kissing eyes darkened with collyrium,

children.text: daśana-vasanam aruṇam tava kṛṣṇa tanoti tanoḥ anurūpam //
children.translated_text: your reddened lip, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, displays a form befitting your [dark] nature.

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.
Your body bears the scratch-marks from the sharp nails of love's battle,
like a victory-inscription of love written on a golden surface inlaid with emerald fragments.

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.
Your generous heart, sprinkled with lac-dye flowing from [her] lotus-feet,
reveals outwardly, as it were, the new sprouts of the tree of <s>Madana</s> (Love).

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.

children.text: daśana-padam bhavat-adhara-gatam mama janayati cetasi khedam /
children.translated_text: The tooth-marks on your lip produce sorrow in my heart;

children.text: kathayati katham adhunā api mayā saha tava vapuḥ etat abhedam //
children.translated_text: how can your body now claim oneness with me?

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.

children.text: bahiḥ iva malinataram tava kṛṣṇa manaḥ api bhaviṣyati nūnam /
children.translated_text: Surely, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, your mind must be even more tainted than [your body's] exterior;

children.text: katham atha vañcayase janam anugatam asamaśara-jvara-dūnam //
children.translated_text: how then do you deceive one who follows you, tormented by the fever of <s>Kāma</s>'s (Love's) unmatched arrows?

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.

children.text: bhramati bhavān abalā-kavalāya vaneṣu kim atra vicitram /
children.translated_text: You wander in the forests to devour helpless women — what is surprising in this?
Even as <s>Pūtanā</s>, you displayed the cruel childhood deed of killing a woman.

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.
The lament of the offended young woman, cheated of love, composed by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> —

children.text: śṛṇuta sudhā-madhuram vibudhāḥ vibudha-ālayataḥ api durāpam //
children.translated_text: listen, O wise ones, to this nectar-sweet [song], difficult to obtain even from the abode of the gods.

children.text: harihari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam
children.translated_text: Go, go, O <s>Mādhava</s>! Go, O <s>Keśava</s>! Do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam //
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one — she who takes away your sorrow.

children.text: tava idam paśyantyāḥ prasarat anurāgam bahiḥ iva
children.translated_text: As I behold this — your heart reddened with the lac-dye from [another] beloved's feet,
as though love were spreading outward,
today, O deceiver, by the shattering of the great burden of my renowned love,

children.text: tvat-ālokaḥ śokāt api kim api lajjām janayati //
children.translated_text: the sight of you produces in me not only grief but even a kind of shame.
Then, to her who was afflicted by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), torn by the passion of love, filled with despair,
who was meditating on <s>Hari</s>'s deeds and withdrawn after the quarrel, a friend spoke:
<s>Hari</s> approaches as the spring breeze blows;
what greater joy could there be in the house, O friend?

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!
Heavier even than palm fruits and most luscious —
why do you render fruitless [these] pitcher-like breasts?

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!

children.text: kati na kathitam idam anupadam aciram /
children.translated_text: How many times has this been told to you, again and again, without delay —
'Do not forsake <s>Hari</s>, who is exceedingly beautiful!'

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!
Why do you despair? Why do you weep in confusion?
The entire assembly of young women laughs at you.

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!
On a cool bed of moist lotus petals,
behold <s>Hari</s> and make your eyes fruitful.

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!
Why do you generate heavy sorrow in your mind?
Listen to my words — they seek no division [between you two].

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!
Let <s>Hari</s> come, let him speak many sweet words;
why do you make your heart so desolate?

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!
May this exceedingly graceful composition by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
the story of <s>Hari</s>, bring joy to the connoisseurs.

children.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye //
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not show pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>!

children.text: snigdhe yat paruṣā asi yat praṇamati stabdhā asi yat rāgiṇi
children.translated_text: You are harsh toward the affectionate one, stiff toward the one who bows,

children.text: dveṣa-sthā asi yat unmukhe vimukhatām yātā asi tasmin priye /
children.translated_text: hostile toward the passionate one, turned away from the one who faces you, O beloved;

children.text: yuktam tat viparīta-kāriṇi tava śrīkhaṇḍa-carcā viṣam
children.translated_text: fitting [indeed] for one who does everything in reverse — for you, sandalwood paste is poison,

children.text: śītāṃśuḥ tapanaḥ himam hutavahaḥ krīḍā-mudaḥ yātanāḥ //
children.translated_text: the moon is the sun, snow is fire, and the joys of play are torments.
Meanwhile, approaching the fair-faced one who was in the grip of tender anger,

children.text: iti nigaditaḥ prītaḥ pītāmbaraḥ api tathā akarot //
children.translated_text: thus instructed, the pleased yellow-robed one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) did exactly so.

children.text: yat gāndharva-kalāsu kauśalam anudhyānam ca yat vaiṣṇavam
children.translated_text: Whatever skill exists in the arts of <s>Gāndharva</s> (music and dance), whatever is <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> meditation,

children.text: yat śṛṅgāra-viveka-tattvam api yat kāvyeṣu līlāyitam /
children.translated_text: whatever is the essence of the discrimination of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love), whatever is playfulness in poetry —
all that, of the learned poet <s>Jayadeva</s>, whose soul is solely absorbed in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
let the wise, full of bliss, examine from the <s>Śrī Gītagovinda</s>.
Of the son of <s>Rāmādevī</s>, born of the lineage of <s>Bhojadeva</s>, <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,
may the poetic art of the <s>Śrī Gītagovinda</s> adorn the throats of the beloved circle beginning with <s>Parāśara</s>.
